{How can Black win material?} 4... g5 {[%wrong There's a better move. Try to
find a good way to break the pin on your knight.] [%hint Break the pin on your
knight and make a threat.]} (4... Nxe4 $2 5. Bxd8 {White is winning. Try again.
}) (4... Be7 $2 5. Bd3 {White is OK. Try again.}) 5. Bg3 {Good move! What's

] [%hint What can you capture?] Great job! Black has an extra pawn for no

{How did Magnus Carlsen gain space on the queenside and fight for the
initiative?} 10. b4 {[%wrong There's a better option. Try again and look for a
strong pawn break.] [%hint Offer a pawn sacrifice to open the c-file.]} (10.
Bxf6 $5 {This is OK, but Carlsen preferred a strong pawn break. Try to find it.
}) (10. c4 $5 {This is playable, but Carlsen advanced another queenside pawn.
How did he do it?}) (10. dxc5 $5 {This is playable, but Carlsen preferred to
attack c5 with another pawn. How did he do it?}) 10... cxb4 {Nice move! How
should you win back the lost pawn?} 11. cxb4 {[%wrong Black is doing well. Try
again and look for a good capture.] [%hint Recapture the pawn.]} (11. Bxf6 $2
bxc3 {Black takes over the initiative with a good position.. Try again and
look for a better capture.}) 11... Bxb4 {Good choice! In the actual game Black
played Nbd7. How would White win material after Bxb4?} 12. Qc8+ {[%wrong
There's a better option. Try again and look for a way to win material.] [%hint
Take advantage of the open c-file and use a skewer to win material.]} (12. Bxf6
$5 {White is doing well, but there's a much stronger move. Try to find it.})
12... Ke7 {Well played! What's next?} 13. Qxh8 {[%wrong Black is winning. Try
again and look for a good capture.] [%hint Capture an undefended piece.] Well
played! White wins a rook and should win the game.} (13. Bxf6+ $5 {White is
doing well, but there's a much stronger move. Try to find it.}) *

{How did Vishy Anand fight back against White's big center?} 14... c5 {[%wrong
There's a better option. Try again and look for a pawn move to fight against
White's big center.] [%hint Advance a pawn to target the d4-square.]} (14...
Rad8 $5 {This is reasonable, but Anand preferred to target the center with
another pawn. How did he do it?}) (14... Rac8 $5 {This is reasonable, but
Anand preferred to target the center with another pawn. How did he do it?}) (
14... Nf6 $5 {This is reasonable, but Anand preferred to target the center
with another pawn. How did he do it?}) (14... exd4 $2 15. Nxd4 {This exchange
gives up Black's influence in the center. Try again and look for a way to
attack the center with another pawn.}) (14... exf4 $2 15. Nxf4 {White's
excellent control of the center offers a significant advantage. Try again and
look for a way to fight for the center.}) (14... c6 $2 15. Raf1 {There's a
more aggressive use of the c-pawn. Try to find it.}) (14... f5 $2 {Advancing
the f-pawn leaves Black's king too exposed. Try to find another pawn move to
attack the center.}) (14... f6 $2 {Advancing the f-pawn leaves Black's king
too exposed. Try to find another pawn move to attack the center.}) 15. dxe5 {
Good start! How should you win back the lost pawn?} dxe5 {[%wrong There's a
stronger move. Try again and look for a good capture.] [%hint Recapture with
a pawn.] Well played! You can continue the sharp struggle between GMs Nakamura
and Anand in the next challenge.} (15... c4 $2 16. Bxc4 {White wins a pawn
with a good position. Try again and look for a good capture.}) *

{One common technique for Black in the Trompowsky and Torre is to take
advantage of the absence of White's dark-squared bishop. What active move did
Anand play here to fight for the initiative?} 16... c4 {[%wrong There's a
better move. Try again and look for Anand's strong pawn sacrifice.] [%hint
Sacrifice a pawn to clear a square for your queen to check from.]} (16... Rad8
$2 17. Qe3 {White's f-pawn may lead to a dangerous attack. Try again and look
for Anand's strong pawn sacrifice.}) (16... Nf6 $2 17. Qe3 {White's f-pawn may
lead to a dangerous attack. Try again and look for Anand's strong pawn
sacrifice.}) (16... gxf5 $2 17. Rxf5 {Black's exposed king will soon cause
problems. Try again and look for Anand's strong pawn sacrifice.}) (16... Qd6 $2
17. Rd1 {White's f-pawn may lead to a dangerous attack. Try again and look for
Anand's strong pawn sacrifice.}) (16... Rfd8 $2 17. Qe3 {White's f-pawn may
lead to a dangerous attack. Try again and look for Anand's strong pawn
sacrifice.}) 17. Bxc4 {Good start! How can a fork win back the lost material?}
Qc5+ {[%wrong There's a better move. Try again and look for a good fork.] 
[%hint Fork White's king and bishop.] Well played! After Rf2 Black can play
Nf6 or Qxc4 with a fine position. Note that the d7-knight is in danger so
Black has no clear win. The game Nakamura - Anand 2011 was eventually a hard-fought draw.} (17... gxf5 $2 18. Rxf5 {White is doing well. Try again and look
for a stronger forcing option.}) (17... Nf6 $2 18. Qe3 {White keeps an extra
pawn and a good position. Try again and look for a strong forcing move.}) *

{Black has left the queen in White's camp for too long and there's a way to
win material. Try to find it.} 6. Rb1 {[%wrong There's a better attacking move.
Look for a good way to target Black's queen and try again.] [%hint Develop and
attack the black queen.]} (6. e4 $2 Qb6 {White has compensation for the pawn,
but Black is OK. Try again and look for a strong threat.}) (6. Nb5 $2 Qxb5 {
Black wins a piece. Try again and look for a stronger threat.}) (6. Na4 $2 Qd4
{Black is doing well. Try again and look for a stronger threat.}) 6... Qa3 {
Good start! How can you continue to take advantage of Black's exposed queen?}
7. Nb5 {[%wrong There's a stronger attacking move. Try again and look for a
winning threat.] [%hint Attack the black queen and prepare a fork on c7.]} (7.
e4 $2 a6 {White is slightly better, but there's a stronger move to win
material. Try to find it.}) (7. Rb3 $2 Qa5 {Black is OK. Try again and look
for a stronger threat.}) (7. f4 $2 c4 {White is slightly better, but there's a
stronger move to win material. Try to find it.}) 7... Qa4 {Great move! How can
you win material?} 8. Nc7+ {[%wrong There's a better move. Try again and look
for a winning fork.] [%hint Fork Black's king and rook.]} Kd8 {Good choice!
What's next?} 9. Nxa8 {[%wrong Black is better. Try again and look for a good
capture.] [%hint Capture an undefended piece.] Well played! White wins a rook
and should win the game.} *

{An early g5 advance is often too aggressive. What surprising move gives White
good chances for an advantage?} 4. Bc1 {[%wrong There's a stronger option. Try
to find the safest square for your bishop.] [%hint Retreat your bishop to its
starting square.] Great move! Black will lose significant time defending the
g5 pawn and retreating the centralized knight if it's attacked. White has a
good opportunity to obtain an opening advantage.} (4. f3 $2 gxf4 {After fxe4
and Bg7 Black is doing well. Try again and look for a way to save your bishop.}
) (4. Bxg5 $2 Nxg5 {Black wins the bishop. Try again and look for the best way
to save the piece.}) (4. Be5 $5 {This is a good move, but most players prefer
the safest square for the bishop. Try to find it.}) (4. Be3 $5 {This is a good
move, but most players prefer the safest square for the bishop. Try to find it.
}) (4. Bd2 $2 d5 {Black has an active position. Try again and look for a
stronger bishop move.}) (4. Bg3 $2 h5 {Black has an active position. Try again
and look for a stronger bishop move.}) (4. Qd3 $2 Nxf2 {After Kxf2 and gxf4
Black wins material. Try again and look for a way to save your bishop.}) (4.
Nd2 $2 Nxf2 {After Kxf2 and gxf4 Black wins material. Try again and look for a
way to save your bishop.}) *

{White has attacked the e4-knight, but Black can fight for the initiative
instead of just retreating. How should you do it?} 4... Qa5+ {[%wrong There's
a better move. Try again and look for a good forcing option.] [%hint Develop
with a check.]} (4... Nf6 $5 5. dxc5 {This is playable, but most people prefer
to insert a check first. How should you do it?}) (4... Nd6 $2 5. dxc5 {White
wins material. Try again and look for a safer forcing move.}) (4... g5 $2 5.
Bxb8 {White wins material. Try again and look for a safer forcing move.}) (4...
e5 $2 5. dxe5 {White wins material. Try again and look for a safer forcing
move.}) 5. c3 {Good choice! How should you save your knight?} Nf6 {[%wrong
There's a better move. Try to find a way to save your knight.] [%hint Retreat
your knight to a safe square.]} (5... Nd6 $2 6. d5 {The knight on d6 makes it
harder for Black to continue development. Try to find a safer knight move.}) (
5... g5 $2 6. Bxb8 {White wins a piece. Try to find a safer move.}) 6. d5 {
Nice move! How can Black make another useful threat?} Qb6 {[%wrong There's a
better move. Try to find a good threat.] [%hint Retreat your queen and attack
the b2-pawn.] Well played! White should retreat with Bc1 to defend the b-pawn.
We will examine another option in the next challenge.} (6... e6 $5 {This is
reasonable, but most players prefer to target the b2-pawn. How should you do
it?}) (6... d6 $5 {This is reasonable, but most players prefer to target the
b2-pawn. How should you do it?}) (6... a6 $5 {This is reasonable, but most
players prefer to target the b2-pawn. How should you do it?}) (6... Qb5 $2 7.
Qd2 {Once White's e-pawn advances the black queen must move again. Try to find
a stronger queen move.}) *
